title: Let agents use grant-scoped team operations and addressed board projections
goal: Make agent communication change a shared, accountable Board through real kernel operations instead of treating conversational messages as authorized work.
scope: Implement Board and Notice with Everyone/agent addressing, Finding, Question, Answer(notice,text), StatusChange and ProposalRef bodies; preserve actual sender, time and versioned references. Arbiter.notice/propose validates references, targets and active grant before committing NoticePosted/ContributionProposed.

Build assignment-to-kernel operation transport for the Scripted and Codex backends delivered by W1-0017/0018: operation name, admitted invocation/assignment, scoped grant and typed arguments/results. Correlate requests and derive identity from the invocation boundary; text cannot impersonate another agent or Runtime.

Route BoardRead, NoticePost, ContributionPropose, OfferSubmit, CommitmentRelease, CommitmentDelegate, ObjectionRaise, StatusNotify, CheckPropose and KnowledgePropose to their owning services. W1 release/delegation/check operations work immediately; later owners add substantive offer/dispute/knowledge behavior, with explicit denials until available.

Expose only the participant’s addressed and permitted Board/*View records, applying hidden-check and sealed-window exclusions below prompts/UI. Merge agent proposals with ContributionPolicy candidates while retaining their rationale/basis and separate kernel decision.
acceptance: An actual Scripted/Codex protocol-fixture assignment reads its Board, posts an addressed question/answer and proposes criterion-directed work; the proposal enters the real candidate consumer and either becomes admitted work or has an inspectable denial.

Expired/revoked/foreign grants, forged authors, unknown refs and disallowed operations cannot mutate Board or other services. Repeating a transport request does not duplicate the committed contribution/notice.

Two participants receive different permitted projections; sealed-window board entries, hidden check data and another agent’s private context are absent from native responses and generated prompts, not merely hidden by presentation.

An agent-originated contribution with new criterion/evidence rationale changes the actual admitted work beyond the fixed baseline, or receives a justified refusal. TeamOperation credentials cannot impersonate a user policy change, stop or continuation request.
context: Authority: ymp-docs/self-organizing-team-domain-model.md, sections 3.4 (Grant, TeamOperation), 3.5 (Board, Notice), 4 (Arbiter), P1/P3/P7, A3/A5 and R-1/R-2/R-10/R-17. Use the approved model with 811a872 semantics and the greenfield baseline in 0c61ff1 and §5.8 for experimental strategy boundaries. Other documents and existing names explain implementation facts only.

Greenfield: create this behavior in the new implementation. Paths below are PROPOSED target modules under the layout owned by W1-0001; only completed prerequisite tasks supply implementation. Prior source, APIs, fixtures and delivery claims are not a baseline.

Create proposed crates/ymp-runtime/src/team_operations.rs and expand the new kernel Arbiter plus Scripted/Codex adapter integrations. W1-0006/0007 provide actual grants/lifecycle, W1-0017/0018 native execution, W2-0001 hidden-data boundaries.

The wire schema/tool exposure is an implementation choice, while named TeamOperation values and kernel ownership are fixed. Native output is an untrusted proposal/request; the kernel derives its actor from the admitted invocation and rejects stale/foreign/revoked grants.

Do not distribute the full journal or hidden payloads. Proposals enter A3’s common candidate list and can change work beyond the fixed control. Agent operations cannot impersonate user stop/continuation or authorized experiment-policy changes.

history.note: Plan new implementation from greenfield baseline 0c61ff1, preserving approved experimental mechanisms, reporting/evidence/recovery rules and explicit prerequisite boundaries.
